A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LUFFY research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark evaluations, training dynamics, component ablations, model extensions and reasoning analyses in Sections 4–5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 retains original empirical results and adds alternative training baselines, Llama experiments, a compute-matched comparison and sensitivity analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed procedure retains mixed-policy advantage estimation, importance weighting with practical πφ = 1, shaping with f(x) = x/(x + γ), and removal of clipping. On-policy clipping removal moves from v1 Section 2.4 to v4 Appendix E.1. The added experiments do not introduce a new LUFFY component.

E1.justification: Training remains based on OpenR1-Math-220k, and evaluation retains the same six mathematical and three out-of-distribution benchmarks. The new Easy/Hard selections and held-out SFT+RL portion change sampling within the existing source and task coverage; additional backbones change model configurations.

E2.justification: v4 Table 1 adds RL w/ SFT Loss and SFT+RL as evaluated comparators for both mathematical and out-of-distribution performance, substantially extending v1's comparison with plain SFT and on-policy methods. The new Llama experiment also includes its corresponding instruction-tuned model.

E3.justification: New protocols include 860-step LUFFY† training to match SFT+RL GPU hours, Llama-specific prompting, 7.3k/25.4k difficulty-filtered training subsets, and an approximately 49k-prompt held-out RL stage for SFT+RL. v4 separately specifies an SFT learning rate of 5e-5, whereas v1 gives an unqualified 1e-6 training rate. The PDFs do not establish whether retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds the Llama Easy/Hard training-failure analysis, a five-value shaping-parameter sensitivity study, and generation-length dynamics comparing RL w/ SFT Loss with LUFFY. Existing component ablations, BLEU analysis, temperature study and case study remain, often relocated to appendices.

E5.justification: v4 introduces paired-bootstrap significance testing with 1,000 resamples in Appendix C.3 and p < 0.05 markers for the headline comparisons in Table 1. v1 reports point estimates without this statistical testing. Bootstrap resampling does not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: Reported math scores change throughout: for example, 7B LUFFY's average changes from 49.6 to 50.1 and SFT's from 47.6 to 44.1, while shared OOD scores remain unchanged. New results cover additional baselines, Llama, sensitivity tests and the longer-budget LUFFY† run, reporting 50.4 math and 61.8 OOD averages. v4 also corrects v1's trained-1.5B averages, which omitted AIME 2025.

T1.justification: The existing convergence theorem and proof move from Appendix A to B.1. New Appendix B.2 adds a first-order Taylor variance analysis and a derivation for exponentially distributed importance weights, providing conditional mathematical support for shaping. The mixed-advantage numerator is also corrected from τi in v1 Equation 2 to R(τi) in v4 Equation 4.

C1.justification: v1 emphasizes improved benchmark performance, generalization and selective imitation. v4 makes successful training of weak models where on-policy RL fails a central abstract claim and explicit contribution. It also expands headline superiority claims to alternative off-policy training methods and highlights computational efficiency.

C2.justification: v4 adds explicit limitations concerning verifiable-reward tasks, model scale and using one off-policy trajectory per question. New interpretations explain Llama training failure through missing positive rewards and attribute SFT-based alternatives' computational overhead to excessively long imitated reasoning. The earlier selective-imitation and exploration interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds the verl/vLLM implementation stack, detailed SFT hyperparameters, baseline construction, difficulty-selection thresholds, subset sizes and Llama prompting. Table 2 newly reports GPU hours and on/off-policy data usage. Several existing disclosures, including hardware and the Qwen system prompt, are relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: v4 updates citations with additional work on RL capability limits, TTRL, Absolute Zero, NFT, reward gaming and statistical testing, while removing some classical RL references. It makes the claim of being first to incorporate off-policy guidance into RLVR explicit. These changes refine the existing positioning between on-policy RL and imitation.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and related work are extensively rewritten, with RLVR replacing much zero-RL terminology and an explicit contribution list added. GRPO and reward background become a separate section. Training details, clipping discussion, ablations and reasoning analyses are reorganized into expanded appendices with a contents list.

P2.justification: v4 merges the separate math and OOD tables into a grouped, shaded Table 1 and adds a resource table and several new plots. The opening performance bar chart is removed, the method diagram is relocated, and Figure 6 is redrawn with an entropy axis and fewer displayed variants. Existing analysis figures and tables are extensively relocated.

improvement.justification: v4 resolves important empirical gaps in v1 through stronger SFT+RL and joint-loss comparisons, matched GPU budgets, and a direct demonstration of on-policy failure on difficult Llama training data. Added significance testing, sensitivity analysis and implementation details substantially improve assessability. Reporting problems remain: Section 5.1 claims a 16.1-point OOD advantage over SFT+RL, although Table 1 supports 13.0 points. This limited error does not outweigh the stronger support for the central contribution.
